[h1]You might love, or hate this game, but it is undeniably well made[/h1]

Changing the review to Positive after ... 480 hours since the last review for a total of 550ish hours?

So. Played through all of he quests, including the Old Peace (except the Venus one), and. Yeah this game is undeniably good.

The first few hours of the game are really, really bad, but it truly gets better. This is a problem for onboarding new players, but it seems to be slowly be ironing out with time.

As someone who has spent a boatload of time playing and seemingly has done in ~550 hours what most people do in 150... Here's some advice.

Just do the story quests. No, Seriously. Ignore most of the fancy grinds. Just, do the Star Chart and do the main quests. You'll unlock exponentially more and more features. But at least it will help you out carve a path towards what you wanna do and focus on, instead of trying to 100%ing every single little thing that pops in your way.

The real discovery was realizing that by the end of the old peace you're still fighting Level 47 enemies and most of the time you're on pre-set warframes and weapons anyway.

If you're starting out, pick a starter frame, get through the star chart, and maybe, ocassionally, get into The Circuit to get a new frame for free.

If you can get through the initial hurdle of the game's first few years (2013-2019), you'll find a surprisingly deep game after the new war. Can't believe i spent so many hours wallowing in my own misery just because i wanted to 100% everything before continuing with more quests... Don't do that.

Also, if you want to play most of the content for free, once you unlock Riven mods... Just unveil their challenges and perform them, then sell those riven mods on the market. Maybe find a calculator to see which ones are more valuable, but... Yeah, if this game does something incredibly well, it is handling FOMO quite well. sell your mods, crack relics, and just get going.

Also, you will find yourself overwhelmed with the amount of tasks at hand at any other week. Duviri, Invasions, Incursions, Archon Hunts, Arbitrations, Void Fissures/Relic Cracking, Nightmre events... Just... Don't try doing all of them at once. The crushing pain of having a timer on you at all times is not worth it. Just have fun with whatever and just focus on one task, and don't be afraid to leave anything half-done. In a few weeks most things come back, and for the limited time events, for 99% of the time, you can get the items from the event elsewhere until the event returns. Pace yourself. And then you'll be able to enjoy the story.

God this review is getting long isn't it? Anyways, the story. Yeah it's incredibly lame and dull up until the first big twist at the end of The Second Dream. From there it opens up and it's... Quite good, it deals with themes of trauma, abuse, healing, improvement and a lot of quite humane subjects. I'd love to spoil the game's plot but there's the Wiki for that and this review is already long enough. You're probably not even reading this anyway.

So yeah. If you can get through the opening hours. Play it and stick to it. It's worth it.

[h1]I no longer stand by my original thoughts, but they are here for openness' sake[/h1]

[h2]The negative review as it stood in 2025 with 60 hours in.[/h2]

I've given this game a good shot at the insistence of some friends, that, to their credit, have been trying to assist me all the way through. But i just cant.

This game has layers upon layers upon layers upon layers of systems within systems within systems within systems within systems, all of them stratified in a seemingly endless pile of grinding and crafting, for components you need to grind and craft for. It just never ends. I've also been told the right way to play the game is to grind for every frame, level them up until they're level 30, then farm every single primed version of each frame until they're also on level 30. Farming and grinding for the sake of grinding and farming, a never ending chore.

Want this game not to become your third shift? Well, cough up 70 euros every two weeks as the new frames enter in rotation. oh but those are the primed ones, make sure to grab 120 euros or so in platinum every two months or so to buy the non primed versions so you can grind those too. And don't forget the weapons.

I've been doing the same three missions in a loop for 60 hours trying to grab the relics needed to unlock the blueprints needed to build a frame and it's related guns, i got the frame but none of the weapons. And even if i did i still need to do a ♥♥♥♥ ton more grinding to get the resources i need, including a resource that only appears in a part of the game i have no access to yet, and will literally disappear from your inventory after you log out. so you better get everything in one go and get those blueprints crafting in one sitting.

I will come back to this review again to tone it down like i've done it. This game has broken me. Christ almighty.

Do you all want to know what the worst part is? [b]underneath that utter and incomprehensible mess of systems there's a great, frantic, chaotic game of blowing ♥♥♥♥ up and slashing foes (or making them swiss cheese with your guns)[/b] but it is stuck so inexorably tight to all of these grueling tasks it's impossible to actually like it. I want to like this game. I really do, i'd not be revisiting this every now and then otherwise. But this is just too much.

You're probably never going to get this review served, but if you do, consider not playing this game. Unless you're able to play the game for 6 to 8 hours at a time every day to ensure you don't run of all of the time-limited stuff before they vault them and you are never able to grab it.

The way this game ultimately forces you into a mindset of "either pay, slave yourself, or miss out" is amoral, cruel and manipulative. No, i don't care that after 36 months you can go and spend 140 bucks on some special currency to buy what you missed in a christmas event, or that if you've slaved yourself away throught those months you can test your luck with random lootboxes (because that's what they are) in hopes you get the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robot or weapon you're looking for. And i'm not getting into the cosmetics. You want your thing to look pretty? god i hope not because you're in for a bad time.

I'm so upset. Do yourself a favour. do not play this game.

[h2]A modified version of the original, scathing 2015 review stands below[/h2]

Apparently things have changed to make things easier for new players but until i've got a chance to test, here's the summary of the old review. 

At the time of writing, you needed an app on your phone that'd wake you at 0300 for nimious tasks. A lot of content but a complete grindfest.

It really didn't respect your time and it is the poster child of Stockholm Syndrome. Ask anyone who has played the game for a while to help you out as a new player and they'll refuse. Ask them to make a new account and they'll outright block you.

It appears they restored a lot of the old content and things are more flexible now, with new frames and loadouts that can help new players, and streamlined a lot of the progression. (Still no 2D solar system map like on the beta though...) 

It's a game that seems to still demand so much from the player. One of these games that want to be the third job you work at each day. It also seems to be a money pit and literally impossible to get through without paying fat cash. Which really pushes back against the idea of trying to catch up with 13 years of content

My account is bugged and it keeps resetting the progress i have. So it's like i never ever started the game despite having tried the beta and the game for a while between 2013 and 2015. That's also something that pushes me back against that. ( years of amazon prime rewards sent to dev/null apparently. )

Can we just get Dark Sector 2005?
I couldn't be bothered to continue waiting for Cross-Save
With all the recent updates I can't stop playing D:

I absolutely hate Freemium RPG's because they flash you with everything you could become from the very beginning and entice you to pay as a shortcut. 
In my playtime the game was cute. The controls were a little weird, but the storyline was cool. In general not a bad game
